items.question: Explain how chaining resolves hash collisions and what determines its operation cost.
items.response: A collision means different keys receive the same hash-table index. Chaining stores items for one index in an additional collection at that index. If keys spread evenly, the typical chain length is proportional to n divided by m. A bounded chain length permits constant-time operations on that chain. A poor hash function can place all n items in one chain, causing linear work.
